title: The Z-Function of a Word

concept.title: For every position, how far the word matches itself from the start; a window [l, r) of the rightmost match is reused
body: The **Z-function** of a word `s` gives, for each position `i`, the length `z[i]` of the **longest common prefix of `s` and the suffix `s[i..]`**. For `aabxaab` the values are `7 1 0 0 3 1 0` (we define `z[0] = n`): the suffix `aab` at the position 4 shares the prefix `aab` with `s`, so `z[4] = 3`. Comparing letters from scratch for every position costs O(n^2) on a word like `aaaa...a`.

Keep a window `[l, r)`: the **rightmost** segment found so far that matches a prefix of `s` (so `s[l..r)` equals `s[0..r-l)`). For a new position `i` inside the window, the letters at `i` are the same as at `i - l` near the start of the word, so `z[i]` starts at `min(r - i, z[i - l])` without any comparison. Only if this reaches the border of the window do we try to extend it by comparing the following letters. When the match extends past `r`, the window moves to `[i, i + z[i])`.

Each direct comparison either moves `r` to the right or fails once, so the total work is O(n). The Z-function and the prefix function carry the same information and can be converted into each other; the Z-function is often more convenient for questions about how a word starts again later.

statement: A word `s` is given. For every position `i` (counting from 0) print the length of the longest common prefix of `s` and the suffix of `s` that starts at `i`; the value for the position 0 is the length of `s`. Print the `n` numbers on one line.
constraints: The word consists of lowercase English letters.
hints: Maintain the window [l, r) of the rightmost match with a prefix.
Inside the window start from min(r - i, z[i - l]).
Extend by comparison and move the window if it grows.

explanation: The window of the rightmost prefix match is maintained; z[i] starts from the value copied near the beginning and is extended by direct comparison only beyond the window.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

s = input().strip()

n = len(s)
z = [0] * n
z[0] = n
l = rr = 0
for i in range(1, n):
    if i < rr:
        z[i] = min(rr - i, z[i - l])
    while i + z[i] < n and s[z[i]] == s[i + z[i]]:
        z[i] += 1
    if i + z[i] > rr:
        l, rr = i, i + z[i]
print(*z)
